summary: Harold G. Coward works in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He earned his doctorate in philosophy at McMaster University (until 1973) and served as a professor at the University of Calgary, director of its press (1981–1983), and director at the University of Victoria.

Harold Hargreaves was an Indologist and historian-archaeologist. After serving as headmaster of Government High School, Amritsar (~1904–1908), he worked at the Archaeological Survey of India as Superintendent (1914) and Deputy Director General (1928–1931), having succeeded Jean Philippe Vogel and John Marshall.

Harold Scheub studied at the University of Michigan (~1956–1960), UCLA (1965), and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (PhD ~1965–1969). He taught at Valparaiso University, Masindi Senior Secondary School, and served as Evjue-Bascom Professor of Humanities Emeritus at Wisconsin-Madison (~1970–2013).
Harold Stewart was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He completed his studies at the University of Sydney and the Sydney Conservatorium of Music.

Harold Walter Bailey worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at the University of Western Australia and Oxford under F. W. Thomas. Bailey taught at SOAS (1929) and held the Sanskrit chair at Cambridge (1936–1967).

Haroon Khan Sherwani was an Indologist and historian. He studied at Aligarh Muslim University (~1905–1909), the University of Oxford (~1911–1914), and under postdoctoral mentor Ghulam Yazdani. He held posts at Osmania University (~1919–1945), Nizam College (~1945–1948), and Zakir Husain Delhi College (~1948–1951).

Harry Falk specializes in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He held a post at the University of Freiburg (~1976–1990) and served as Professor of Indology and Director at the Free University of Berlin (~1993–2012).

Hartmut Buescher works in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Copenhagen under Chandrabhāl Tripathi, later holding a post at Copenhagen and an affiliation with the Royal Danish Library (attested 2007).
Hartmut Scharfe was an Indologist and linguist who completed his doctoral studies under Paul Thieme. He later held a post at the University of California, Los Angeles.

Hartmut-Ortwin Feistel is an Indologist who headed the Katalogisierung der orientalischen Handschriften in Deutschland (attested 1989), worked in the Prussian State Library's Oriental Department (attested 1992–1994), and served as project director at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2008).

Haruhiko Masaki is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Gakushuin University (~1957–1961) and completed master's and doctoral coursework at the University of Tokyo (~1961–1967), later serving as professor at Nagasaki University (attested 1988).

Haruka Yanagisawa was a scholar of Indology and history-archaeology. He held academic posts at Chiba University from around 1974 to 1988 and subsequently at the University of Tokyo from around 1988 to 2007.

Harumi Hirano Ziegler is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. She completed both her MA (awarded 1994) and her PhD (awarded 2001) at the University of California, Los Angeles, where she was supervised by Robert E. Buswell Jr.

Harunaga Isaacson works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Groningen and Leiden under Hans T. Bakker, Tilmann Vetter, and Albrecht Wezler. He held posts at Groningen, Oxford, Pennsylvania (2002–2006), Hamburg (from 2000), and the IIBS (attested 2026).

Harushige Takatsu was a linguist and Indologist. He studied under Naoshiro Tsuji at the University of Tokyo and at Oxford. He held teaching posts at the University of Tokyo (1938–1948) and served as humanities dean and professor at Musashi University (1968).

Harvey B. Aronson specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. Supervised by Richard Hugh Robinson and taught by scholars including Stephan Beyer and Geshe Lhundub Sopa, he held a professorship at the University of Virginia (attested 1988) and co-directed the Dawn Mountain Center.

Hasmukh Dhirajlal Sankalia was an Indologist and historian-archaeologist. He studied at University College London from around 1934 to 1936 and served as a professor at the Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute from around 1939 to 1973.

Haya Akegarasu was a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar. He studied under Manshi Kiyozawa and Shimei Futabatei at Otani University and Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, later serving as head of administration at Higashi Hongan-ji (~1951–1954).

Hayao Kawai worked in religious studies. He studied at Kyoto University (~1948–1952), taught at Tenri University (~1962–1972), served as professor at Kyoto University (~1972–1992), and was director general of the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (~1995–2001).

Heather Stoddard specializes in Tibetology and history-archaeology. She studied at SOAS University of London (~1964–1967) under D. C. Lau, as well as under Nicole Vandier-Nicolas and Samten Gyaltsen Karmay.
